# Neon Editorial

Category: `professional` · Audience: Engineering managers, writers, researchers, and architects · Output: static HTML/CSS/JS

A luxury developer-magazine aesthetic — deep navy, lavender-purple accents, and editorial serif headings for engineers who also write.

A narrow reading column with a serif narrative, numbered case-study essays, dated publications, an understated CV, and a letter-like contact close.

## Design tokens

| Token | Exact value |
| --- | --- |
| accent | `#818cf8` |
| background | `#07080f` |
| text | `#e8eaf6` |
| muted | `#7986cb` |
| surface | `#0f1120` |
| border | `#1e2240` |
| Body family | 'Geist', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif |
| Heading family | 'Newsreader', ui-serif, Georgia, serif |
| Font styles | body: sans; heading: serif |
| Density | spacious |

Text, muted text, and accent contrast against the background / card surface:

| Foreground | Background | Surface |
| --- | --- | --- |
| text | 16.69:1 | 15.63:1 |
| muted | 5.79:1 | 5.43:1 |
| accent | 6.70:1 | 6.28:1 |

The preset text combinations exceed 4.5:1. Decorative borders are not used to convey essential information. Custom colors need a new contrast check; this palette check alone is not a full WCAG conformance audit.

## Default content and order

Hero → About → Projects → Writing → Experience → Contact

All identities, organizations, metrics, and work below are fictional examples. Links use example.com. The default footer labels them as illustrative; replace them before removing that label in Theme controls.

### 2. About — Bridging code and clarity.

I'm Mira — an engineer who can't stop writing. After eight years building products at startups and agencies, I found that the best technical decisions come from understanding the problem in plain language first.

I write to understand. I build to verify. The two habits make each other sharper.
